messages:
sophia: quick sync — we're about to flip the reduced-residency TTL change in the handshake proto. question: how do we 'grandfather' tenants who signed residency contracts (EU-only) without adding months of rollout ops? :thinking:
kevin: my worry is eviction cascades. shorter TTLs -> more frequent lease swaps -> more write retries at the edge.
olga: agreed. for EU-only tenants we can't risk a cross-region handoff during a live write window. we should allow a per-tenant override to keep the old TTL until we migrate.
lucas: per-tenant override is fine but ops will hate the long tail. can we do a migration wave: (1) opt-in fast migration for low-risk tenants, (2) automated probe + canary for medium-risk, (3) manual for contractual-tenants?
infra-bot: deployment plan created: canary=10% traffic in eu-west-1, probe window=4h, fallback->region-fallback-policy v2
sophia: proposal: introduce 'residency_grandfather' tag on tenant metadata. default=false. when true, runtime bypasses handshake TTL reduction and also disables auto-evict for that tenant until flag cleared.
maria: we already have a metadata flag for 'residency_lock' used during onboarding. can we reuse it instead of adding new fields?
olga: reusing is fine but semantics differ. 'residency_lock' stops migrations; 'grandfather' explicitly preserves old handshake behavior (TTL and eviction thresholds). I'd prefer explicit name.
kevin: operational concerns: how do we audit which tenants are grandfathered, and how do we ensure we don't forget to clear the flag after migration? suggest adding 'grandfather_expires_at' timestamp.
lucas: +1. Also add a sys-telemetry signal when a handshake fallback occurs because of grandfathering so SRE can see counts in Console.
sophia: here's a minimal config snippet we can add to tenant metadata:
```
residency_grandfather: true
residency_grandfather_expires_at: "2026-06-01T00:00:00Z"
```
kevin: runtime change: handshake.proto: add optional bool residency_grandfather and optional int64 expires_at_unix. handshake handler: if residency_grandfather && now < expires_at -> treat as legacy TTL (60s) and no auto-evict.
olga: question: legacy TTL 60s ok? current plan reduces to 10s in most regions for better failover. keeping 60s for grandfathered tenants will increase cost but should be acceptable per contracts.
maria: legal wants explicit opt-in from tenant owners before we flip them to the new behavior. ops needs a CSV export of all grandfathered tenants.
sophia: action items:
- kevin: PR for handshake.proto + runtime check (ETA EOD)
- lucas: Console telemetry + tenant export (ETA 2d)
- olga: migration waves plan doc (ETA 3d)
- maria: coordinate legal signoffs and customer comms (ETA 5d)
kevin: small nit: while we're adding fields, let's also add a 'grandfather_reason' string enum (contract, compliance, customer_request) so we can filter.
lucas: +1
infra-bot: note: rolling update will mark nodes as draining when handshake changes are live; expect 5–10% increase in in-flight request retries during canary window
sophia: thanks. anyone opposed to leaning conservative: default to keep tenants on legacy behavior unless they actively opt-in to fast path? we can still nudge them via Console.
olga: conservative default seems safer for enterprise contracts. :thumbsup:
maria: legal: agree
kevin: ok. I'll gate the PR behind a feature-flag so we can flip per-tenant via Console without code rollbacks.
sophia: perfect. I'll post the migration wave doc once olga's draft is in. quick follow-up: do we need a separate SLA for grandfathered tenants? they expect no cross-border writes, so we should ensure their SLOs are explicit.
lucas: we already annotate per-tenant SLOs in Billing; may need small update. adding 'residency_class' label should be enough.
infra-bot: action logged: 4392101111/handshake-grandfathering-plan created
sophia: thanks team — closing this thread, will reopen if blockers show during canary.
